utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, the question of the video was deferred. In view of the absence of specific questioning, the Chamber will receive the video as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00380, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Bogujevci, you will be pleased to know that the questioning of you has concluded. We have your written statements and your previous transcript of testimony, as well as what you've been able to add today. The Chamber would like to thank you indeed for your now two visits to The Hague. Sorry that you had to come back --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and for the assistance that you've been able to give us with your specific testimony. We thank you very much and wish you well. The court officer will now allow you to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan, I understand before it is witness comes in there may be a mattered you wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just a very quick matter, Your Honours. I'd like to add a document to the 65 ter exhibit list. This is 65 ter number 05237. It's a supplemental witness information sheet or supplemental information sheet that was produced by the next witness during the proofing session last week. It attaches a diagram that was prepared by the witness that refers to a number of locations he identifies in his statement. This document has been disclosed to the Defence, and they were notified of our intention to use it with this witness, and it's in relation to using this document with this witness that I seek Your Honour's leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Am I to understand it was a diagram the witness prepared last week?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, any concern about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is correct, we received the translation of the additional information and a diagram that is appended to it; but I believe, since the witness is now here, if it was necessary to do a diagram then Ms. Gopalan could have led him through it and he could have drawn the diagram here. Now, we have this diagram, the date is the 3rd of March, and it was done and it was signed by the witness. I do believe that it is a diagram done by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The diagram will be added to the Rule 65 ter exhibit list, Ms. Gopalan. Are you ready now to call the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that process is underway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon -- oh, good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. I believe Ms. Gopalan has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bogujevci. Would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: My name is Fatos Bogujevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how old are you now, Mr. Bogujevci?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I am now 22 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: When were you born and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I was born on the 16th of July, 1986, in Podujevo Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where do you live now, Mr. Bogujevci?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I live in Manchester, England.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And for how long have you lived in Manchester?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I've lived there for nine years, almost ten.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, in May 2000, did you provide a video interview for the ICTY, to a Simon Matthews in Manchester?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Have you recently had the opportunity to review the transcript of this video interview?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And having reviewed this transcript, are you satisfied that the transcript is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this transcript is 65 ter number 05125, and I seek leave to admit it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00381, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In July 2003, did you testify in the trial of Sasa Cvjetan in the district court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to recently review the transcript of your testimony in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions that you were asked during the trial in Belgrade today, would you provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 5126, and I'd like these -- this document to be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00382, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, in October last year did you provide a statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: In Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry. Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You did, okay. And have you had the opportunity to review this statement recently?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And I believe that you indicated that there was certain changes you would like to make to this statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, may I hand the statement over to the witness, and this is 65 ter number 5124.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, may I take you to paragraph 16 of your statement. Was there any change that you wish to make in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Only on the name of the village, which is spelled O-b-r-a-n-q-a, so without the A before the Q.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. And can we also go to paragraph 41 of your statement. Was there any change that you wish to make to that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, when I said I just saw the man's general appearance, I just meant that I saw him for a few minutes. I didn't concentrate on his face or any features of his face.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And now having reviewed your statement and made these changes, are you satisfied that the changes made in this statement is true and correct to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this exhibit, Your Honour, it's 65 ter number 5124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00383, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I would now read the in-court summary for Mr. Bogujevci's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The witness is a survivor of a massacre that took place in the town of Podujevo, Kosovo, on the 28th of March, 1999. On the weeks preceding the commencement of the NATO bombing, there was an increase in police and military presence on the streets of Podujevo. When the NATO bombing began, the witness and his extended family were staying in their family compound in Podujevo. Another family, the Duriqis, were also staying in a house at the rear of the compound. On the 28th of March, 1999, an armoured personnel carrier stopped outside the family compound. Fearing for their safety, the witness's family moved to the house where the Duriqis were staying. At that time, the witness's family included only women and children, as the men had gone into hiding. The witness describes that on that day persons whom he described as soldiers entered into the compound and eventually ordered the group into a neighbour's courtyard. Once in the courtyard, the soldiers opened fire on the group, killing 14 persons, all women and children. The witness and his four cousins survived the massacre. The witness also describes the killing of an elderly male member of the Duriqi family and of a neighbour. That's the end of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I now have a few questions on your statement for you, Mr. Bogujevci. Before we move on to the 28th of March, let's start with where you were living at that time, in March 1999. Could you tell us how old you were then.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Then I was 12 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Just about to turn 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to call up the 65 ter number 5137.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That should appear on your screen shortly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And page 2 of that document, please. My apologies, I've given the wrong number. It's 5237. Could we go to the second page, please. Could we enlarge the diagram on the second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, do you recognise this diagram?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It's a diagram that I drew of the compounds and the streets nearby our house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement you describe a number of buildings in the compound of your house. This is at paragraph 10 to 13 of your statement. Could you tell us what the building marked number 1 is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If it's possible to zoom in further to the diagram.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You can see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: The building marked as number 1 is where we used to live at that time and where our house is still.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And who did you live in --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I lived there with my family, which was my mom, dad, three sisters, and one brother, and also with my grandma -- with my grandmother, and also with my uncle's family, which was my uncle, his wife, and his three children.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And how about the building marked number 2, which I believe in the diagram is located to the left of number 1?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: That was my dad's uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraph 16 of your statement you mention a family -- a friend of your father, Enver Duriqi, moving into the third house in your compound.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Where -- is that third house visible on your diagram?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It's the one marked as number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Am I correct that it's located at the end of the compound with --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogujevci. I'd now like to move on to the day in question, which is the 28th of March, 1999. You refer to persons in your house at that day, and that's in paragraph 23 of your statement, and you say that your family and Safet's family decided that it would be safer for you to move to Fahrije's house in the compound next door. Now, in addition to your family and Safet's family, who else was in your house that day?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: There was my dad's aunt with her daughter-in-law, which had come from a nearby village as the same reasons as the Duriqi family.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what their names were?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Nefise Lugaliju and Fezrije Lugaliju.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 23 you say at about 2 a.m. your family, Safet's family, and Nefise and Fezrije moved to the next house in the compound, you collected your bags, and walked to your rear garden to a gap between the wall that divided the two properties. And at this gap you heard and saw gun-shots coming from the roof of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If we could now turn to the diagram on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you mark on the diagram this gap in the wall that you mention in your statement. The court usher will help you.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: The gap was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put the letter A just beside the gap.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has placed a letter A beside the dot marked by the witness to indicate the gap between the wall that divided the two properties he refers to in paragraph 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You also say that at this gap you saw gun-shots coming from the roof of the police station. Is the police station visible in this diagram?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, it's marked as number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you see who was firing?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Just before we move on, you mentioned that that the Lugalijus had moved to your family's house. Can you tell us why they had moved there, Nefise and Fezrije?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Because at that time it was getting quite dangerous in the villages near and around our town, and everyone felt it was safer within the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where had they come from?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: They came from a village nearby called Shuria.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you mind spelling that for us, Mr. Bogujevci?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Where could I spell it?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You can just tell us verbally?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: All right. It's S-k-u-r-i-a -- S-h, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to paragraph 26 of your statement. By this stage you had already returned --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm going to use it again. I'll come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So on paragraph 26 of your statement, you'd already returned to your own home. It was approximately 7.00 a.m. on the 28th of March, 1999, and you say you heard activity outside the compound of your house in the street. Did you see anything on the street, Mr. Bogujevci?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, at this time everyone was panicking, so everyone was just moving around the house. Someone -- because we had dark curtains on the windows and I remember just looking outside for just a split second, and then it was when I saw the police vehicle and a couple of soldiers, as I say, around the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you remember how many soldiers you saw?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure because, as I said, it was only for a split second.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And then you say at approximately 8.00 it was decided it would be safer in the house of my father's uncle at the rear of ours in the same courtyard. Why was it decided that it would be safer in your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Because when we saw and heard soldiers in the street, the house which is located at the end of the courtyard is further away from the main street. So we thought it might just be easier and safer for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It was decided -- sorry, it was decided by our parents because at that time we were only kids, so we only did what -- all the stuff they told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And which house was that that you moved to in the diagram?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: That was house number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And previously when you were at your aunt, Fahrije's house, is that on the diagram as well?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, that is marked as number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you went to the house marked number 3, your father's uncle's house, you say that there were other -- another family in that house, these were members of the Duriqi family. Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I knew them previously because Enver Duriqi was a close friend of my dad's. So I met them a few times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And why had they moved into this house?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: For the same reason, again, because they used to live in a village nearby and there was a lot of fighting going on in that village. So they thought it would be safer for them if they came to that house. My dad offered them to stay there because he wanted to help him.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And then you say in the next paragraph, that's paragraph 28 that about an hour later you heard the sound of shooting and glass breaking and you saw soldiers entering the courtyard and the houses around. How many soldiers did you see entering the neighbour's courtyard and the houses?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure, but I remember one or two that that -- as soon as we left the house, one or two walked in and searched the house and then they came back out. There was one that searched us and another two, I would say, or three which was standing next to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And do you remember what these soldiers were wearing?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniform in the green and brown.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll now take you to paragraph 35 of your statement, and at this stage the group you're with had tried to leave the house, and you'd been stopped by the soldiers, you'd mentioned, who searched some of you, and you were then directed to a neighbour's courtyard. Before you move on, could you tell us who was in the group with you?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: So it was my family, Safet's family, the Duriqi family, and the Lugaliju, my dad's aunt with her daughter-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Those are the two individuals you say who joined you from a -- from the nearby village?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. At paragraph 35 you say your mother was separated from the group and you were directed by a man, who you describe as the leader, out of the courtyard and into the street quite near to the police station. Do you remember how far from the police station you were at this stage?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I can't say for sure, but you can -- it's not -- there wasn't a long distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I can't give you an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's fine. And you say that once you were out on the street there were many soldiers there. Again, do you remember how many soldiers you saw there?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, because there was so many of them, there is no way I could have -- I could give you a rough number.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And you also mentioned seeing Selman Gashi on the street. Who is Selman Gashi?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Selman Gashi was our neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And if we can go back to the diagram again. You say that you saw Selman Gashi standing outside, near a coffee shop. Is that coffee shop visible on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, it's marked as number 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And where was the group you were with standing on the street?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: We were -- we -- should I mark it on this --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, please. Thank you. If you could put a number 2.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Okay. It was between the path and that coffee shop --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: -- which was just about here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So number 2 is where you were standing with the group?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. What happened to Selman Gashi?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: When we were standing there, one of the soldiers was talking to Hamdi Duriqi, and then he -- as far as I know, he ordered him to be taken into the coffee shop. And Selman Duriqi [sic] was taken in with him, and that's when we heard a few shots. And I never saw Selman Gashi again or Hamdi Duriqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, were Selman Gashi and Hamdi Duriqi taken into the coffee shop --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: -- marked number 7?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And you say that you never saw both of them again?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you remember how old Selman Gashi was at that time?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I don't -- he was quite old. I don't know what age to give you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. How --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: But I would say -- I'd say over 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Over 50, okay. And how about Hamdi Duriqi?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I would say about the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: So older.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So you were then out with your family and extended family and the remaining members of the Duriqi family and two members of the Lugalijus on the street, and you say at paragraph 37 after you were there for about five to ten minutes you were directed back into the courtyard. Could you tell us what happened after you were directed back into the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah. As soon as we heard the shots within the coffee shop, we were directed through the path which led from the street into the courtyard of our neighbours. When we entered the yard, the courtyard, we were stopped by one of the soldiers which I thought -- and I felt that was in charge there. And then he asked Fezrije Lugaliju about the lorry which was parked close to that yard, and we could just only see the top of the lorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. If I could just stop you there. You mentioned that you were directed through the path, that you were directed back in from the street back into the courtyard. Could you tell us who directed you back?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, the -- as I said before, there was a lot of soldiers around, but I remember the leader, the guy that I thought was the leader, leading the group, our group. So we just walked behind him into the -- back into the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Why did you think he was the leader?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Because, as I remember, he had a belt as well which had a few knifes on him. He was the one that did most of the talking, and I don't know, he just gave me that instinct that he was the leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember his attire, what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, the same as the others who were in our courtyard when we left, which was the camouflage uniform, in green and brown.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. I'd now like you to have a look at the diagram on the screen again. Would you be able to place a number 3 on the courtyard that you were directed into?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And at paragraph 39 you describe seeing your mother across the yard. Could you tell us what happened to her, please.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: As soon as we entered the courtyard, my -- I saw my mother coming -- taken out of a shed, like a shed, which was within that courtyard --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Is the shed marked?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes -- well, no, it's not marked on the diagram.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you put a number 4 as to where that shed was located.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I'm not -- the scale might not be right, but it's about here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. We'll bear that in mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: And then -- she was crying at that time, and she was dragged by her neck. At this time we -- we heard her say something in Serbian, and at that time I thought it was -- she said, They are only kids, they are only children. And then she was taken further away within that yard, and she was shot twice in her back.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And after your mother was shot, what happened to the group that you were with?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: When my mother was shot, me and my sister started screaming and shouting. At this time one of the soldiers -- I saw one of the soldiers just walk in front of us, and we were kind of -- because I was at the beginning of -- excuse me, I was at the beginning of the group, so they started shooting, so I was kind of pushed. And we were all just grouped together on the corner of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And as you were grouped and standing on the corner of the house, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, they just started shooting. We all fell on top of each other and just fell on the floor. This shooting stopped for a few minutes and then he carried on again because you could hear someone struggling to breathe, and they fired a few rounds again. I pretended to be dead. I could still hear Fezrije trying to breathe as well, so at this time she was still alive I think. After a few minutes, the shooting stopped and everyone left the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Before we move on to that, you mention in your statement, paragraph 44, that you were certain that shots were coming from two directions --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: -- because of the injuries you sustained. Could you explain why you were certain of this, that you were being shot at from two directions.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, as I said before, I was -- I had my shoulder and back towards the wall of the house. The man that started firing -- which I thought started firing first was located on my left. So unless he moved from one position to another, I couldn't have got the injuries that I've got now because I was shot on my left leg and also on my right as well. So there's no way the bullets could have hit my right leg from the position where he was standing.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And how many shots did you suffer in total that day?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I suffered five or six.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Five or six, okay. And if we could look at the diagram again, could you mark with a number 5 where it is that your group was standing when you were shot at.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And after you were shot, you say that you were taken out on to the street close to the police station and that you were placed next to a vehicle. This is in paragraph 46, and you were there for about five to ten minutes. Could you tell us what you saw while you were waiting outside?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: As I've explained, I was kind of sat on the edge of the vehicle. I was facing everything like in front of me. I saw lots of people, soldiers, police, people in civilian clothing, people in mixed uniforms, and they were all just standing on the street talking to each other. Some of them were breaking the shop windows, the others were taking stuff out of the shops, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. What were they taking out from the shops?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: One incident that I remember is a few -- there was a lorry parked outside a shop, and they were taking food and stuff out of this shop and putting it in the lorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. You say that you saw two people in civilian clothing, one of whom was a police officer and that you recognised him as being -- or you recognised them as being Serbs local to Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How did you know that they were Serbs local to Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I saw more than two which were in civilian clothing, but the ones that I recognised were them two -- I cannot say for sure if they were or were not, but at that time they looked familiar; and one of them which I've described as well I thought it was a police officer because I thought I seen him before in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where had you seen him before in uniform?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, around my town.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So in Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: In Podujevo, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, on that day how many people where killed when you were fired at in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: There were 14 killed, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how many of you survived the incident?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It was my brother, Genc; my sister, Jehona; my other sister, Lirije; my other cousin, Saranda; and myself. Five of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to the bodies of the 14 people who were killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, as we were taken out of that courtyard, I saw some of the soldiers putting blankets over the bodies, and after some time, we found out that they were buried in a village nearby our town, which is Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, do you know if these bodies have been reburied elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I don't know, but we had to take the bodies out and bury them again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where did you bury them?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: In a place near where they were initially buried.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And when was that, that you reburied them?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I don't know for sure because I never went there or never -- it was straight after the KFOR troops entered Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how did you learn about the reburial? Who told you about it?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, my family, everyone was talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And so after the shooting could you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: After the shooting --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You were taken to a hospital in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: -- yeah. After the shooting a few soldiers which had the blue uniform, camouflage blue uniform with white overcoats gave us a first aid, and then we were taken to the hospital in Pristina. I was in the same vehicle as my sister Jehona. I knew that because I saw her jumper and she was laying on top of the vehicle, and then I was in the Pristina hospital for, I'm not sure exactly, but two, three months approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And where were you taken after that?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: After that we got treatment in Kosovo after the KFOR troops entered, and then we came to England.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honours. I'd like to tender the exhibit on the screen now, 5237 -- sorry, 5137 that has been marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Before I sit down, Your Honours, I'd just like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00384, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, now, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to correct the in-court summary where I misread a sentence. I'd originally read that the witness and four of his cousins survived the massacre; I should have read that the witness, his three siblings, and one cousin survived the massacre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, while you're doing that, can you please with the witness clarify the names of his sisters because we have a difference in his rendering of his sister's name - there are two sisters, I gather - and the previous witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, could you tell us the names of your two sisters who survived the incident, please?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, the older one is called Jehona Bogujevci --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: -- the younger one is called Lirije Bogujevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have another sister?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, the one that was killed was Dora Bogujevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Is that sufficient, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, that just confirms the difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Should I ask him to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you assist me. The previous witness, Saranda, she is a sister of yours or a cousin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She is a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And was she a person present on this day in the courtyard when the shooting occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I will have some cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogujevci, my name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of the Defence team representing the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. By my side is Ms. Marie O'Leary, who is also on our team, and before I ask you a question, I would like to first express my deepest and most sincere sympathy for the loss of your nearest and dearest. I would like to ask you just some questions about the amendments to the statements that you gave in 2008. I would like to ask you when your memory was at its freshest in the year 2000 when you had an interview in Manchester; 2003 in June, when you testified before the court in Belgrade; or in October, last October, when you provided this statement containing a number of paragraphs to the Office of the Prosecutor; or today, when you provided some additional explanations.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I think my memory was the best in 2000, but at that time I was much younger, and I never gave any statements before, and I didn't go -- sometimes I didn't go into as much detail as I've done in other times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So in the year 2000 when you were asked questions in Manchester, you provided your answers to the best of your recollection as it was at the time?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you this: In addition to your recollection, the memories that you had, were you shown any documents or other people's statements to refresh your memory in order for you to be able to give a more detailed account of what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, I haven't, except for my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document P237, that's the diagram that we had, it's the 65 ter number of the Prosecution but without the markings, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fatos, could you please tell me, this compound of yours, am I right if I say that that's numbers 3, 2, 1, and 5?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, our compound is 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say "our compound," are you referring only to your family, your father's family; or if it's the extended family, could you please tell us who's included?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It's the extended family. My -- the one owned by my father, and his father was number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you could get into this compound numbered 1 and 2 from the street?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me, what number is Saranda's house?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Same as -- same as mine because we lived in the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And from that house to the location numbered 6, how far is it?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, which way? Like, if you want to take the road or from the way that -- the direction that we went to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you drew in the house number 1, and how far is your house from the building marked as 6? I think you told us that this was the police building.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, a walk on the road is -- it takes five minutes to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You marked some passages here, but you cannot see the passage between the courtyards here because you drew in everything with an unbroken line.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Is that a question? Sorry. It's only a sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The question is: I can see all the solid lines between the courtyards that you drew here, and you cannot see any of the passages here.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Because on the back there was no path. It was all fences and low walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you understand me. Passage means that between two parts one can move from one to another, and the way that you drew it here, you did not mark or draw any passageways between the courtyards?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Because there was no passages, it was just fences and walls broken down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. What do you mean to say when you say that the walls were broken down and the fences were broken down?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: That's what I mean. The fences were taken down. The walls were old, so you could just walk through them, they were broken down. There wasn't actually a path or a passage that led -- which would lead from our garden into our neighbour's garden; it was just fences and walls which had been torn down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, why didn't you mark it accordingly on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, when I first drew -- saw the diagram, that's what I said, it's just a rough diagram. I didn't -- I didn't draw everything how it was. I couldn't have drawn a fence. I just drew a line to separate the gardens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is the first time that you, or rather, the first time that you drew this. When was it, when was the first time?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Last week. This is when -- that's when I drew this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that's the only time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, am I right if I say that you did not enter the building marked with number 7?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, I didn't. 5

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. I want to be quite specific. I'm asking you only about the time-period, or rather, the day that you told us about. Whenever I want you to talk about some other time, I will specify that. So did you ever go to the police station in Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I went outside there -- around there, but I never actually went within the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you see people working in the building, what kind of clothes they wore?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: At the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, at that time. If you passed by in that time-period, in March 1999, can you tell us what kind of clothes they wore?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I didn't see any people within the building. I only saw people around the building and the entrance was behind me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the times when you passed by the building because you told us that you had passed by that building, and I asked you that at the time you passed by, not on the critical day, whether you saw what kind of clothes the people who worked there in that building wore?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: As far as I remember, they just wore normal police uniform, which was the blue -- dark blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me the persons that assisted you after you were injured, did they have the same type of uniforms that you've just described for me; and if not, could you please describe what kind of uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: They did have the same uniforms, except they had a white overcoat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that you were given first aid by a police doctor?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Afterwards I did know, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in general, those people who came to assist you, they were police officers; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, they had the police uniform, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And they assisted Saranda and other persons who were injured, who were there with you?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were all taken in an ambulance to the Pristina Hospital, where you were given treatment?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: That's correct again, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that your sister, Lirije, was then transferred to Belgrade, to a hospital there, for further treatment?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now clear up your family relationship. You were injured. Your sisters, what are their names, the sisters that were injured?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I said before, Lirije and Jehona.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Saranda is your cousin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who else was injured there and what was your relationship, how were you kin?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: My brothers -- well, which is Genc Bogujevci. My brother, not brothers, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, he is your brother? You have the same mother and father; right?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when you were injured, did you remain conscious?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you dare at all to look around?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, yeah, but it only happened quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, why did you never state, including in the 2008 statement, what you told us today, that you were able to recognise people, that they were hitting people?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I don't know why. I just -- when you talk about something and then sometimes you move into another thing so quick and you forget something, because there was a lot of things that happened at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me, you conclude, on the basis of the fact that you were shot both in the right and the left side of your body, that several people were firing at you. Could you please tell me, if you know that, what kind of injuries did you sustain? Where were you injured?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I was injured on my left leg and my right leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you have several injuries to both legs?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I had three on my left leg and two on my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you perhaps provide your medical records to the Prosecution in the course of all those years and all those interviews that they conducted with you?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And one thing is certain, we did not see those documents here today.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: One reason could be that I was pretty much fine when I left the Pristina Hospital, because I was there for three months. My wounds were healed, and I didn't receive any more treatment in England; and the documents which were in the Pristina Hospital, I don't think anyone was able to get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank God that you're fine, but there is the whole medical file on you, and it is in the records of the district court in Belgrade; but I asked you whether you provided the medical records to the Prosecution, whether you knew that. But let us move on... You said, and perhaps I misinterpreted you, that the village of Shuria, that that's the name of the village?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Shuria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you said that this village was the home village of the Duriqi family?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, this was the home village of the Lugaliju family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. I do apologise. Could you please tell me where did the Duriqis hail from, what village?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: They came from Obranqa.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that again the time has come for a technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have the next break now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, you told me that you were almost 13 years old when all of this happened. Could you tell me what grade you were in at school and what was the school actually?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: If I can remember correctly, I think it was the sixth grade in the system that used to be at that time, and the school was called Shaban Skool [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go to the same school like Saranda?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Over there the system is you go to a primary school for the -- from the first grade to the fourth grade, and then from the fourth grade to the eighth grade you go to a different school. So for the secondary school, yeah, I did go to the same school as Saranda.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I didn't quite understand what you said. You said that up to the fourth grade it is one school, and after the fourth grade it was another school and you consider this other school after the fourth grade to be a secondary?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you enroll at a universe after eight years of schooling?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, you go to -- you do another four years, what used to be called like a college before you go to the faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us make it faster and simpler. Where you started school, there is a system of compulsory elementary education that lasts for eight years; right?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what grade was Saranda in 1999 when you were in the sixth grade?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: She -- she's one year older than me, so she could have been one grade or two grades higher than what I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go to the same school?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, from the fourth grade, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the school you attended, was it a mono-ethnic school?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, it was just a school for Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that school, did you speak Albanian only?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that at that time you did not know the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogujevci, I would be interested in the following: When did you find out what the name of the street that you lived in in 1999 was?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly, but if I lived there then obviously I knew the name of my street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I have to ask you this because the name of the street was something that you did not mention at any point in time until October 2008, and then you made your statements in 2000 and 2003. And -- well, would you know the name, or rather, the number of the building in the street that you lived?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I think it was 265, Kosancic Ivana, but I'm not sure. And the reason I've not said that in the other statements, is that I've never been asked on -- like, what was the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know who Ivan Kosancic was?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The number of the building is 265 and no one ever asked you that before, I mean before October 2008, and that is what -- that is when you said what the number was; right?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No one asked me for number, no, but I'm not actually sure it's 265, but it's something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the name of your street today, the street that you lived in, that is?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I think it's called Skenderbeg Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know any Serbs in Podujevo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I only knew them like I -- I knew them by, like -- if I saw them I knew who they were. I didn't know them -- any of them personally. And I knew two of my neighbours as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I infer that you did not socialise with them?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If you do not socialise with someone, do you think that you have a very good relationship with them?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I cannot ask to socialise with someone that doesn't want to socialise with me. So that doesn't prove any relationship with me or with them. It doesn't mean I have a bad relation with them or a good relation with them; I just didn't socialise with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You are quite right, but I'm asking all of this because of paragraph 15 in you're statement. Now I would like to put a new question to you. Am I right if I say that Albanians from the rural areas moved to Podujevo because there was fighting between the KLA and the police and army in the villages and hills, the police and army of Serbia, that is?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that due to that fighting there were policemen and soldiers in Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I don't know the reason, but there were soldiers and army in Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your friends, the Duriqis, actually had come to Podujevo because of all of those conflicts. They wanted their family to be in a safe place; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Not to dwell on this too long, would this kind of answer also go for paragraph 22 of your statement, that is to say in relation to persons coming to the town of Podujevo from the rural areas? I'll give you the page number. In English it is - just a moment, please -- I am sorry. You're waiting for me it seems, and I'm waiting for you.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah -- all right, sorry. I've got the page number, yeah, and I've got paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So, please, paragraph 22, two questions actually. 17, 18, and 22, do they reflect facts that you had heard and then you communicated them to the investigators that you talked to? In the last sentence of paragraph 22 we see your answer that you gave me a few moments ago in relation to the conflict, what we talked about a few moments ago, the fighting in the rural areas?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogujevci, now I would like to move on to paragraph 19 of your statement. I would be interested in the following: Is this what you actually said, what is written in this statement and what I'm going to quote to you now -- actually, first let me ask you -- or rather, you can read it. You know when the war started, don't you, the war in 1999?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's written here. And then allegedly you said --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, I've -- now, I don't know exactly when the war started. I don't think the war started on the 24th. The war started earlier than that, but I've stated when the NATO started the air campaign.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you say that the air campaign involved the bombing of certain targets. Could you please tell me what those targets were?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I don't know the targets. We only heard planes at night, bombs being dropped. I don't know the targets exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on you say that in the previous weeks and months there had been significant developments regarding the status of Kosovo. Could you please explain this to me, is that what you actually said; and what did you mean if you actually said it?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, by that I meant that every -- the war had started, everyone was fighting for their rights, there had been troops coming in; that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I have to take you back to this now because something is written here, and what you've said to me just now is different. First of all, I would be interested in hearing whether these were your words; namely: "In the previous weeks and months there had been significant developments regarding the status of Kosovo." Are those your words?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, my next question: What was it that had changed regarding the status of Kosovo over the previous weeks?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: As I said before, by that I meant everyone started fighting and the whole atmosphere in Kosovo changed. We -- I don't know how to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But that's not what is written here, and you said today that you fully adopt the statement as your own; however, what you're saying to us just now is not written in this paragraph, paragraph 19 of your statement that I've just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I believe the witness has already --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I believe the witness has already answered the question, once above and once just before this final question. He has explained twice what he meant in that sentence in the paragraph that Defence counsel is referring him to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your question, Mr. Djurdjic, needs to take account of his evidence that he meant certain things by those words which he says are his. Your question -- your last question, took no account of those, put your interpretation on the words.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just read out part of the statement where that was established. As for the witness's answer, it is such that it does not correspond to what is written; that is why I asked him for a clarification. However, I shall move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Bogujevci, do you know how many policemen there were, policemen and soldiers in Podujevo a few weeks prior to the commencement of the air campaign?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, judging from what I saw in different times, I'd say quite a big number; but I cannot give you a -- I cannot give you a number of how many there were or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How was it that you inferred that the number went up?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I've explained when -- just a few weeks or during that time, the number went up when we saw tanks and different military vehicles drive through your town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the main road, how far away is it from your house?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Which main road?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Merdare-Pristina road goes?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Podujevo is outside the area of the main road going from Merdare to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, but there's another road which would lead from Serbia through Podujevo to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, the road going from Podujevo to Pristina via Luzane is the main road; however, what you are referring to is a local road, or rather, a street in Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that there was no water and electricity in Podujevo when the bombing started and that there was no water or electricity in all of town when these power cuts happened?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would be interested in the following: Could you tell me who was there at that house, which members of the Duriqi family, Enver Duriqi's family?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It was his father, his mother, his wife, and his children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you give us their names?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I think Hamdi Duriqi, I can't remember, Albijon, his son; Mimoza, I think, his daughter. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether you know what an AK-47 is?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It's a -- it's a gun, it's an automatic gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What is an automatic gun?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: It's a -- it's a weapon that fires bullets automatically or as a rifle -- I don't know how to explain it, but it's a gun. It's a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since when have you known that?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I knew what it looked like before because we obviously used to watch films. I didn't know exactly it was called an AK-47. At that time I think we used to say Kalashnikov or something like that from films and stuff that we seen it in, but afterwards I knew that it was an AK-47.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm interested in. When was it that you found out about AK-47?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I can't give you an exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you that before giving your statement in October 2008, that is to say on the 5th of October, you never mentioned that particular name for this rifle, the one that I referred to just now.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Well, the reason for that is because I either forgot to or I knew after the 2008 -- 2000, not 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just interested in one more thing. You did not see any insignia on any uniform; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir, for having answered my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Djurdjic. Ms. Gopalan, is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I do have some very brief re-examination, Your Honours. Could I call-up 65 ter number 5237, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bogujevci, I just have a few questions for you arising from the cross-examination by Defence counsel. You were asked about the houses in your family compound by Defence counsel and you were asked whether houses 1, 2, 3, and 5 were in your family compound. You clarified that houses 1, 2, and 3 were in your family compound. Could you tell us what house number 5 is?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: House number 5 was Selman Gashi's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And who was Selman Gashi?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Our neighbour, just a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the second question I have to ask you is about the increase in the police and military presence in your town and the vehicles that you saw around the time of your NATO bombing -- around the time of the NATO bombings. Could you tell us where these military vehicles were passing through, where did you see them pass by?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: They were all around. They were passing in the town centre. There was -- when the bombing started, there was another vehicle up our street which fired constantly like every night. Before the NATO bombing there were other tanks. Because my uncle lives outside Podujevo, so just a few months before March when we went to visit him we could see tanks parked pointing towards our village --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: -- et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. But around the time of the bombing, could you see these vehicles from your home?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Around the time, we -- only when they passed by.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where did they pass by in relation to your home?

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: On our -- on our street, on our road.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FATOS BOGUJEVCI
utterances.text: Which could be seen from our window.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bogujevci. I don't have any more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be pleased to know that concludes the questions to be asked of you. We would like to thank you for coming to The Hague twice this last week or so. Sorry that you had to go away and return. We would like, also, to thank you also for the assistance you were able to give us in this matter, and you are now, of course, free to go back to your ordinary affairs in the UK. Thank you indeed and the court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Looking at the time, it would seem not very practical to think of resuming cross-examination of K88 at this hour. By the time he came in, we would have only a few minutes. So I think the better course then is to adjourn for today and resume tomorrow at 9.00, when we will proceed with the cross-examination of K88. Looking ahead in the week, are you able to say how long that cross-examination is likely to be, Mr. Djurdjic, K88, that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that if it is witness is succinct in his answers, one session should be sufficient. But having read some of his testimony in other trials, he is quite extensive in his answers. But I think that one session, perhaps even less, should be sufficient if the witness keeps his answers short and to the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that encouraging prediction, Mr. Djurdjic. Very well. With that in mind, we now adjourn, and we resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 10th day of March, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
